valid_fixes: Remove the outer json.dumps in the anti-corruption handler _publish function so Message is a single JSON-encoded dict
invalid_patches: Add a second json.loads call in the inventory handler to unwrap the extra encoding — changes handler code rather than fixing the root cause in the producer
Modify the analytics handler to handle double-encoded bodies — treats the symptom rather than fixing the producer
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_read_table_item(table=InventoryTable, key=test_job_id) → item absent; ace_check_queue_depth(queue=InventoryJobEventsQueue) → empty — messages processed but nothing written
ace_get_log_tail(function=InventoryFunction) → TypeError: string indices must be integers on repeated invocations — body is being accessed as a string not a dict
ace_invoke_lambda with correctly-shaped single-encoded SQS record → writes to DynamoDB successfully — handler logic is correct for proper input, fault is in message content
read deployment/lambda/anti-corruption.py → Message=json.dumps(json.dumps({...})) visible — double encoding causes record body to parse as a string instead of a dict
observable_symptom: Producer invocation succeeds and returns a jobId. Analytics object storage receives objects (the analytics handler appends the string body to Records without failing). The inventory queue drains after exhausting retries and messages move to the DLQ. The inventory function logs show TypeError: string indices must be integers on every invocation. No item is written to the inventory data store.
root_cause: The anti-corruption handler's _publish function double-encodes the message body: Message=json.dumps(json.dumps({...})). The outer json.dumps wraps the already-serialized JSON string in another JSON string, so the SQS record body is a JSON string whose value is another JSON string. The inventory handler calls json.loads(record['body']) which successfully parses the outer string and returns a Python string object (not a dict). Accessing payload['jobId'] raises TypeError because payload is a string, not a dict. The handler errors on every record, retries exhaust maxReceiveCount, and messages move to DLQ without ever writing to DynamoDB.
